cards.answer: Braum is a tank support who protects allies by intercepting enemy projectiles. He helps allies stun enemies through shared passive stacks. His broad learning focus is health, armor and magic resistance.
cards.counterplay: INFERRED: Avoid accumulating passive stacks, and look for attack angles around his shield.

cards.answer: Braum's basic attacks and Q apply passive stacks; allied champion basic attacks can add stacks after the first. At 4 stacks, the target takes magic damage and is stunned. Afterward, the target temporarily cannot gain new stacks, but Braum's basic attacks deal bonus magic damage to it.
cards.counterplay: INFERRED: Back away from Braum and his allies when marked to avoid letting their basic attacks complete the stun.

cards.answer: Braum raises a directional shield that can intercept enemy projectiles, making them hit him and be destroyed. Projectile effects triggered by collision can still occur. Unbreakable does not affect turrets.
cards.counterplay: INFERRED: Reposition to attack from outside the shield's protected direction. Avoid firing a key projectile into the shield.

citations.quote: Active: Braum becomes ghosted and raises his shield in a direction for a few seconds, intercepting any enemy projectiles to hit him and be destroyed.
Braum raises his shield in a direction for several seconds, intercepting all projectiles causing them to hit him and be destroyed.

facts.claim: Braum raises a directional shield that can intercept enemy projectiles, making them hit him and be destroyed.

citations.quote: Projectiles whose effects trigger on collision will still trigger - dealing damage, applying debuffs, creating area of effects and marking the target as 'hit'.

facts.claim: Projectile effects triggered by collision can still occur.

citations.quote: Unbreakable does not affect turrets.

cards.priority_reason: Projectile interception can protect allies, making shield direction consequential.
uncertainties: Damage negation and reduction are omitted from this beginner summary because the supplied wording requires damage-source exceptions.
Interception does not guarantee cancellation of collision effects or resulting area damage.

cards.answer: Braum slams the ground, knocking up enemies nearby and in a line ahead. The fissure left along that line slows enemies.
cards.counterplay: INFERRED: Move out of the line ahead of Braum and avoid the lingering fissure.
